Hi Daniel — great to meet yesterday. Quickly addressing your bullets and attaching our DPA + current subprocessors list: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf, subprocessors_list_2026.csv. High level: 

- No-training commitment: Redwood can offer a contract clause restricting use of customer content for model training or improvement. For hosted customers we can enable a persistent "no-train" tenant flag which isolates requests from model training pipelines.

- Evidence: We provide request/response export on-demand (CSV export) and can produce token-level tracing and audit logs showing the no-train flag was set for a date range. For enterprise customers we can also provide retention policy configuration and a one-time export of historic request metadata.

- Ownership: Our standard position is that customers retain ownership of their prompts and outputs. We will add explicit language to the DPA and terms that assign output/prompt ownership to MedSure and exclude it from model improvement.

- Subprocessors and transfers: See attached list. Most infra subprocessors are US-based; we use EU-region cloud providers for EU data and can contractually restrict processing to those regions. For any non-EU transfer we support standard contractual clauses and can discuss additional safeguards.

Next steps: Naomi, Rishi — I’ve looped you in for legal/security confirm. Daniel/Ellen — if this sounds OK I can prepare a redline of the DPA and a short mutual action plan for procurement. Ben — FYI on pricing impact if MedSure requires dedicated isolation.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Daniel/Ellen — quick legal/security notes after my review: 

1) DPA redline: We will add a clear "No Training / Model Improvement" clause that prevents Redwood and its subprocessors from using MedSure content for model training, including derivative model weights and shared embeddings. That clause will specify the scope (customer content, metadata) and duration of the commitment.

2) Evidence and auditability: We can offer the following evidence types: a) activity logs showing the tenant-level no-train flag, b) on-demand export of request/response payloads (subject to retention/PII rules), and c) a signed attestation that we have not used MedSure data for model improvement during the contract period. Please advise which of these MedSure legal/security needs for procurement.

3) Subprocessors: CSV includes roles and locations. For subprocessors that process telemetry or logging, we will provide access controls and only provide data required to operate the service. If MedSure needs a substitute subprocessor process (e.g., right to object), we can negotiate a mutually agreeable workflow in the DPA.

4) Data residency: We can commit to region-restricted processing for EU/US workloads and will include SCCs for transfers outside the EEA. For particularly sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pools) — that also simplifies evidence collection.

I will prepare a short set of redline changes and an audit-evidence checklist — please confirm which evidence artifacts you require.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
